page.title: Compilers and interpreters
page.desc: Turning source text into something that runs: lexing, parsing, semantic analysis, intermediate representation, optimisation and code generation, or interpreting an IR directly, or JIT-compiling it at runtime.
page.intro: Turning source text into something that runs: lexing, parsing, semantic analysis, intermediate representation, optimisation and code generation, or interpreting an IR directly, or JIT-compiling it at runtime.

synapses.text: Front end (lex, parse, check) produces an IR; the middle end optimises it; the back end emits machine code for a target.
CPython compiles to bytecode then interprets it; V8 interprets bytecode and JIT-compiles hot functions; the line is blurry.
Dead-code elimination and loop transformations are only valid if the program avoids undefined behaviour, which is where surprising C output comes from.

children.title: Lexing and parsing
children.desc: Lexers turn characters into tokens; parsers turn tokens into a syntax tree according to a grammar, by recursive descent, LR tables or Pratt-style precedence climbing.

children.title: LLVM
children.desc: A compiler infrastructure started by Chris Lattner at the University of Illinois in 2000 (released 2003): a typed IR plus optimisers and back ends shared by Clang, Rust, Swift and many more.

children.title: JIT compilation
children.desc: Compiling at runtime using observed behaviour: V8, the JVM's HotSpot and PyPy start interpreting, profile hot code and compile it with speculative optimisations that deoptimise when assumptions break.
